About us

Waikato District Council is the local government authority for the Waikato district. Like your business, we think about the future and we work to make sure our district is the kind of place we all want for generations to come. Our vision is that we work together as a district to build liveable, thriving and connected communities as our district grows. To achieve this we work in partnership with the community to ensure the planning, direction and management of our resources meets the present and future needs of the people and the environment.

    Partnerships come full circle for the now three-legged Enza. Enza was found wandering the streets of Huntly with a badly damaged back leg. Sadly, no one came forward to claim her, and despite every effort, her leg couldn't be saved. That's where long-time partners Fundraising for Impounded Dogs stepped in. Thanks to funds raised and donated by our Animal Control team's Pound Pup Pool Party back in April, Enza was able to have the surgery she needed at GT Vets. Partnerships like these help make second chances possible, ensuring dogs like Enza get the care they need and the opportunity to find the loving forever homes they deserve.

    Around 70 students from Horotiu School marked their 9th year of annual tree planting by placing 1,200 native seedlings along the Te Awa Cycleway this week. Days like this don’t happen without a lot of people pitching in behind the scenes. Big thanks to Enviroschools and Trees for Survival for working with the school to help students grow 600 of the seedlings themselves at school. Not forgetting our team at WDC, along with partners Cushman & Wakefield, Citycare Property, and NZ Police plus the teachers and parents who all helped support the day and make it happen.

    Our contractors removed a large amount of illegally dumped rubbish, furniture, household items, and toys in and around the MacDonald’s Road stormwater pond in Pookeno. Illegal dumping costs our environment and council: polluting our streams, rivers and lakes, and costing thousands of dollars to remove. Stormwater ponds play an important role in our stormwater system, slowing down the flow so sediment and pollutants can settle or breakdown naturally, which helps return cleaner water to our rivers, lakes, and streams. We all have a role to play as kaitiakitanga, and protecting our environment for future generations. If you see illegal dumping, please report it on Antenno or via our website, https://lnkd.in/dBaUfKHT
